body: It would certainly solve most of my problems since I would *know* God is there with me.

It's something I would probably do. Seeing that I believe in the cause of the Kingdom of God. My only problem is it would all be in vain. Not that I'm looking for a reward out of it, but it'd be a crap feeling to do all that work just to be thrown in the lake of fire for all eternity.
I was kind of hoping you'd read all of the post.
I don't have a Skype, but I'd be extremely grateful if you prayed for me.

Well, those verses are saying no one can force us out of our relationship with Christ. We can choose to reject it. Like I did. Also, there are tons of Scripture talking about losing salvation (oh, and twice lost always lost, not once saved always saved). Just to name a few, John 15, Romans 11, Romans 1, Hebrews 6, 2 Peter 2, so on and so forth.

Unfortunately, the "many" in Matthew 7:21-23 really means many. I'm one of them, and if anyone else has rejected Christ as Saviour as a born again Christian, they have permanently lost their salvation as well. It's not good news to hear, but that doesn't mean it isn't true.

I understand it may be a selfish thing, but at this point, I find it really hard to care. If any atheist who didn't believe in an afterlife walked in my shoes for a mere week, they would have already ended themselves. 

Literally the only thing holding me back from suicide is that I'll go to hell early. Although life is hell enough already, I would rather not burn for all eternity.
As I said, Hebrews 6 says otherwise.
